title: EU Taxonomy User Guide: A user guide to navigate the EU Taxonomy for sustainable activities
scope: Explains how to understand and apply the EU Taxonomy for sustainable economic activities
overall_summary: Provides a practical explanation of what the EU Taxonomy is, how it fits within the EU sustainable finance framework, and how companies and financial institutions can assess the alignment of their economic activities with the Taxonomy criteria.

role_in_sustainable_finance: Describes the EU Taxonomy as a cornerstone of the EU sustainable finance framework and a key transparency tool.
Explains that the Taxonomy provides a common language for what is considered environmentally sustainable, supporting the European Green Deal and EU climate and energy targets.
Highlights its use by both financial and non-financial undertakings, as well as by policymakers and regulators.
main_objectives: Help users understand the structure and key concepts of the EU Taxonomy.
Provide a simple, step-by-step approach for determining whether economic activities are Taxonomy-eligible and Taxonomy-aligned.
Clarify how Taxonomy disclosures relate to other EU sustainable finance regulations such as CSRD and SFDR.

environmental_objectives.name: Climate change mitigation
environmental_objectives.description: Activities that contribute substantially to reducing greenhouse gas emissions or enhancing removals, consistent with a net-zero pathway.

environmental_objectives.name: Climate change adaptation
environmental_objectives.description: Activities that reduce or prevent negative impacts of climate change, or help people and nature adapt to changing climate conditions.

environmental_objectives.name: Sustainable use and protection of water and marine resources
environmental_objectives.description: Activities that improve the status of water bodies and marine ecosystems, or reduce pressures such as pollution and over-abstraction.

environmental_objectives.name: Transition to a circular economy
environmental_objectives.description: Activities that increase resource efficiency, extend product lifetimes, enable reuse and recycling, and reduce waste.

environmental_objectives.name: Pollution prevention and control
environmental_objectives.description: Activities that prevent or reduce emissions and releases of pollutants to air, water and soil, and that limit exposure to harmful substances.

environmental_objectives.name: Protection and restoration of biodiversity and ecosystems
environmental_objectives.description: Activities that conserve, restore or enhance ecosystems, habitats and species, and that reduce drivers of biodiversity loss.

alignment_conditions.title: Substantial contribution to at least one environmental objective
alignment_conditions.summary: An activity must make a meaningful positive contribution to one of the six environmental objectives based on technical screening criteria, or qualify as an enabling or transitional activity under the climate objectives.

alignment_conditions.title: Do no significant harm (DNSH) to other objectives
alignment_conditions.summary: While contributing to one objective, the activity must not significantly undermine any of the other environmental objectives, evaluated using DNSH criteria in the delegated acts.

alignment_conditions.title: Compliance with minimum safeguards
alignment_conditions.summary: The activity must be carried out in alignment with minimum social and governance safeguards, including OECD and UN guidelines on responsible business conduct and human rights.

alignment_conditions.title: Compliance with technical screening criteria
alignment_conditions.summary: The activity must meet the specific quantitative or qualitative thresholds and process requirements defined in the relevant Taxonomy delegated acts.

taxonomy_navigator_tools.name: EU Taxonomy Compass
taxonomy_navigator_tools.purpose: Provides a visual representation of sectors, activities and criteria included in the delegated acts.
usage: Look up whether a particular activity is covered by the Taxonomy.
Identify which environmental objective the activity relates to.
View high-level descriptions of substantial contribution and DNSH criteria.

taxonomy_navigator_tools.name: EU Taxonomy Calculator
taxonomy_navigator_tools.purpose: Guides users through reporting obligations and KPI calculations.
usage: Determine which KPIs must be reported by a non-financial undertaking.
Apply the Taxonomy rules to classify the share of the company’s activities and investments that are eligible and aligned.
Generate summary tables consistent with disclosure templates.

taxonomy_navigator_tools.name: FAQs repository
taxonomy_navigator_tools.purpose: Central collection of frequently asked questions on the EU Taxonomy and its delegated acts.
usage: Clarify interpretation questions on eligibility, alignment and DNSH assessments.
Check applicability thresholds and transitional arrangements.
Stay updated on new clarifications issued by the European Commission.

taxonomy_navigator_tools.name: EU Taxonomy User Guide
taxonomy_navigator_tools.purpose: Entry-level explanation and practical roadmap for applying the Taxonomy.
usage: Understand the basic concepts and terminology used in the Taxonomy Regulation.
Follow a step-by-step alignment assessment process.
See examples of how the Taxonomy interacts with other parts of the EU sustainable finance framework.

step_by_step_alignment_process.title: Identify economic activities
step_by_step_alignment_process.description: List the company’s main economic activities and map them to relevant activity descriptions used in the Taxonomy.

step_by_step_alignment_process.title: Check Taxonomy eligibility
step_by_step_alignment_process.description: Determine which activities are covered by the Taxonomy delegated acts and therefore potentially eligible.

step_by_step_alignment_process.title: Determine substantial contribution
step_by_step_alignment_process.description: For each eligible activity, assess whether it meets the substantial contribution criteria for at least one environmental objective.

step_by_step_alignment_process.title: Assess DNSH criteria
step_by_step_alignment_process.description: Evaluate whether the activity complies with the ‘do no significant harm’ criteria for the remaining environmental objectives.

step_by_step_alignment_process.title: Check minimum safeguards
step_by_step_alignment_process.description: Confirm that the company’s policies and practices meet the required social and governance safeguards.

step_by_step_alignment_process.title: Calculate aligned KPIs
step_by_step_alignment_process.description: Calculate the proportion of turnover, CapEx and/or OpEx associated with Taxonomy-aligned activities based on the results of the previous steps.

step_by_step_alignment_process.title: Prepare disclosures
step_by_step_alignment_process.description: Compile the results in the prescribed Taxonomy disclosure templates, ensuring consistency with other reporting frameworks such as CSRD and SFDR.

example_use_cases.title: Non-financial company using the guide to prepare Taxonomy disclosures
example_use_cases.summary: A manufacturing company identifies which production lines correspond to Taxonomy-defined activities, checks alignment with climate mitigation criteria, and calculates the share of turnover and capex that are Taxonomy-aligned.
relevance: Supports preparation of CSRD-aligned sustainability statements.
Helps communicate the green share of revenue and investments to investors.
Enables comparison with peers in the same sector.

example_use_cases.title: Financial institution assessing client portfolios
example_use_cases.summary: A bank uses the User Guide and Navigator tools to assess the Taxonomy alignment of its corporate loan book and to compute portfolio-level alignment indicators.
relevance: Supports SFDR and prudential disclosure requirements.
Informs product design for green loans and bonds.
Identifies sectors and clients with higher or lower alignment potential.
